You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

Output changes seeds to4, expands 7 across upper-left region: rows0-1 cols0-3; row2 cols0-3 except seed4 at c2; row3 cols0-1 and3; row4 cols0-2 plus seed4 c3; remaining bg. Demo8 9x28 bg8, border6 top-right col27 rows0-1 and left col0 rows4-5; color5 seeds at (4,6),(5,8). Output fills color5 rectangle rows0-1 cols0-26; rows4-5 fills horizontally cols1..6 / 1..8 respectively, seed coordinates become4; other cells mostly bg. Demo6 18x27 bg9, color2 bars top-left cols0-2 and bottom cols13-15; seed1 at (12,13). Output vertical line color1 at col0 rows1-12; seed->4 at (12,13); line color1 col13 rows13-16 to bottom bar. Demo5 8x11 bg2, bars color5 top-right cols7-10 and bottom-left cols2-5; seeds1 at row4 cols2,4; output seeds->4, extensions down cols2,4 rows5-6; copies/extended vertical traces at cols7,9 rows1-7. Other examples similarly bars and marker patterns, so likely geometric propagation/reflection from seeds toward and between border bars, not simple whole-row/column fill. Avoid guessed indiscriminate fills. In test instance bars were color3 at top row cols9-11 and bottom row cols0-2, lone 6 seed at (18,9); eight guesses failed (vertical col9, projected col0, full fill, horizontal row). Useful if task recurs: reason with endpoint geometry and seed pattern carefully; request demos valuable.')
